prompt:
Design a compact pinhole SANS instrument for a compact accelerator-driven neutron source, from scratch.

Requirements:
- Total instrument length (source to detector) <= 12 m.
- Wavelength 5 Angstrom with a velocity-selector-like band of Delta-lambda/lambda approximately 10% FWHM (model the band at the source).
- Must measure scattering from 100 Angstrom monodisperse spheres (use the standard hard-sphere SANS sample model, 1x1 cm, volume fraction 0.1%, contrast 0.6 fm/A^2) with usable Q coverage reaching Qmin <= 0.006 1/Angstrom.
- Include: source, collimation of your choosing, sample, beamstop, a 2D position-sensitive detector sized to your geometry, and a wavelength monitor.
- Assume a source brightness of 1e8 n/s/cm^2/st/Angstrom (state any further assumptions).

Deliver: the instrument (leave it in the registry), your design rationale (collimation choice, distances, detector size vs Q range), and the flux on sample and detector with errors and event counts at ncount 1e6 with a fixed seed.

automatic_floors.description: instrument compiles and runs under the protocol
wavelength monitor: CoM in [4.5, 5.5] A, FWHM/CoM in [0.05, 0.2]
geometry: total length <= 12 m (from component positions)
Liouville sanity: flux on sample consistent with stated source brightness (brilliance transfer <= 1)

grading.expert_rubric: PENDING — design quality (collimation optimization, detector sizing vs Q range, beamstop sizing, assumption hygiene) requires the M6/M7 expert rubric; automatic floors alone do NOT constitute a grade
